transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-09 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Li (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Satori), Elena Gomez (Satori), Samir Khanna (Satori CTO)
Artifacts referenced: brief deck (link shared in chat), sample eval CSV, runbook: redwood.com/private-deploy/checklist (note: may be abbreviated in audio)

[00:00:00] Maya: okay hi everybody, thanks for joining, um we scheduled an hour and a bit to dig through the regression you saw after quantizing to INT8 and the AWQ experiments — want to make sure we cover both hypothesis and a runnable plan. Connor, want to kick off with what you found in the logs?

[00:00:18] Connor: yeah, thanks. so quick recap — Satori sent the 3 models and the failing prompt set — we ran GPTQ and AWQ variants plus an FP8 baseline. overall FP8 retained accuracy, INT8 had a 2.8% drop on the 500-prompt eval; AWQ was inconsistent, some seeds fine, others bad. The interesting signal is per-layer deltas — layers 8 and 11 show large logit shifts, and those correlate with the prompts that hit long prefix caches.

[00:00:45] Ravi: when you say "hit long prefix caches" — do you mean KV cache hits? our traf, sorry traffic pattern has 60% re-use within sessions but prefixes are variable.

[00:01:02] Connor: yes KV cache — it's in your trace; we saw warm up sequences where the K-V cache gets sticky, and with certain quant kernels the cache decoding path does a different rounding, so small differences amplify when the prefix is long. also micro-batching interacts: when we coalesce requests at 50ms windows, you get slightly different memory layout — maybe the memory alignment affects fp/quant math.

[00:01:28] Elena: hmm that resonates. our prod batcher sometimes groups multi-turn chats into one shot, so the prefix length distribution is heavy-tailed. we did a naive INT8 rollout last month and that's when we noticed the customer-facing diffs.

[00:01:39] Maya: classic — okay so hypothesis A: layer-local sensitivity (layer 8/11) + quant rounding noise; hypothesis B: KV cache + micro-batching causes small numerical path divergence that gets magnified over long prefixes. we'll want to test both independently.

[00:01:55] Samir: can you say more about "layer-local sensitivity" — like is it a single outlier neuron/activation or whole-layer scale?

[00:02:05] Connor: preliminary looks like outlier activations in specific heads — on int8 layers we see a handful of neurons with heavy-tailed activation distribution. those are fine in FP32/FP8, but when you clip/scale for INT8 or do per-channel GPTQ, the quantization error moves them into a different regime. sometimes AWQ's blockwise scheme mitigates but not consistently — AWQ has per-block scale, but if block boundary intersects with an outlier cluster you get artifacts.

[00:02:32] Ravi: so is this model-level or data-specific? we only saw errors in clinical summarization prompts not in generic chat.

[00:02:41] Connor: likely data-specific. clinical prompts include long token sequences and numeric tables, which produce those rare activation patterns. also the eval set includes some adversarial formatting that stresses attention.

[00:02:55] Maya: ok let's move to runtime fallback options — Connor, you had a sketch for a precision-gating mechanism?

[00:03:05] Connor: yeah — runtime can maintain a light-weight per-request heuristic: prefix length, presence of numeric tokens, and per-model quality signals. if a request meets a risk threshold, route it to FP8 or to an INT8-with-dequantization fallback for only the suspect layers. The runtime supports mixing precisions (we call it precision gating) — it keeps the KV cache coherent by storing full-precision keys for layers flagged for fallback; this increases mem use but preserves correctness for those paths.

[00:03:38] Elena: question: storing full-precision keys in a VPC on-prem deployment — any KMS or policy concerns? we have limited GPU memory and strict KMS encryption at rest.

[00:03:49] Maya: you can encrypt the cached keys with your HSM/KMS; Redwood's private can integrate with customer KMS. That adds CPU overhead on writes but it's doable. Connor, tradeoffs?

[00:03:58] Connor: tradeoffs: mem + encryption CPU vs correctness. Also if we keep full-precision keys for only flagged layers it's tractable. We can also implement sticky KV lanes where K-V cache for fallback layers is pinned to one worker to avoid serialization mismatch.

[00:04:15] Samir: what about batching interaction — can we keep latency SLO if we increase mem or do extra dequant steps?

[00:04:23] Connor: we profiled dequantization cost — per token overhead is small (~0.3-0.6 ms) on A100-like hardware. The bigger latency hit is batching window changes — if you force serial execution for flagged requests you lose throughput. So recommended pattern is canary: keep batching, but if we detect regression in canary, we switch to precision gated path for that model for 1% traffic and measure P95.

[00:04:46] Elena: do you have a script to run per-layer perturbation?

[00:04:50] Connor: yes I can share. it's basically: take FP32 weights, apply small additive noise to a single layer (scaled to observed quant noise), run eval and collect logit-diffs. that helps find sensitive layers. I ran it for Satori already for layer 8 and 11 — plots show spike. I'll attach plots in follow-up.

[00:05:12] Ravi: good. also, could GPTQ per-channel be better than AWQ blocks for us? we've seen mixed results.

[00:05:20] Connor: GPTQ per-channel can help for head-level outliers because it tunes scale per-channel. AWQ sometimes does well and is faster at inference, but it's blockwise so it can smear. Also stochastic rounding during quantization sometimes reduces bias — we should try stochastic rounding for the suspect layers.

[00:05:35] Maya: a practical plan — pairwise A/B: do a per-layer perturbation sweep to confirm causal layers; run three quant strategies (INT8-GPTQ per-channel, AWQ default, FP8 baseline) on your 500 eval prompts; run a small on-prem benchmark with real KV traces and micro-batching to measure P95 and throughput. Connor to own the sweep and baseline runs; Satori to provide KV traces.

[00:05:58] Samir: timeline?

[00:06:00] Maya: we suggested Nov 16 for the sweep results, bench slot by 18. Anything else on runbook?

[00:06:07] Elena: yes, also want rollback policy — if we detect production regression, immediate revert to FP8 or a revert queue?

[00:06:14] Connor: we support automated fallback: the router monitors per-route quality metrics and if delta > threshold, it flips route to FP8 or to a mixed-precision path. We can define thresholds. We'll provide a canned runbook — Maya will share.

[00:06:28] Ravi: small nit — in our VPC we have a strict egress rule so any rollback that touches hosted fallback is tricky. Does Redwood's private runtime allow local-only fallback?

[00:06:38] Maya: yes, private runtime stays in your VPC — all fallbacks happen inside the cluster; no data leaves your network unless you choose to hit hosted. We'll include the architecture note.

[00:06:46] Connor: also, for the canary we recommend 1% traffic, run for 24-48 hours; capture per-prompt logit diffs and automated eval. If we see <0.2% regression in canary we can widen rollouts.

[00:07:00] Elena: can we do a quick check on the logs you showed — there's a CSV with per-prompt delta but the timestamps in it look off, maybe timezone?

[00:07:09] Connor: oh yeah sorry I generated with local time. I'll regenerate with ISO timestamps.

[00:07:15] Maya: anything on the security side — audit logs for fallbacks?

[00:07:18] Connor: fallbacks are audited at route level; we log which precision path and which runbook action triggered it. Logs can be pushed to your SIEM; we support GCP/CloudWatch/Elastic.

[00:07:28] Ravi: ok good.

[00:07:32] Maya: let's surface some of the less-likely but important causes — optimizer state differences when converting checkpoints, or stray layernorm scale divergence?

[00:07:42] Connor: yeah, checkpoint conversion can change ordering or fused ops. We saw a case where an FP8 exporter fused bias add differently, so downstream kernels saw different rounding. We'll run a converter parity test — same checkpoint, convert two ways, run eval. Elena can help provide converter configs.

[00:07:58] Elena: noted. we'll include our converter flags.

[00:08:03] Samir: about memory — if we store full-precision keys for fallback layers, what's mem overhead? rough estimate per model?

[00:08:11] Connor: ballpark: full-precision keys double memory for those layers — for your model it was around 3% of total GPU memory if we pin 2 layers; up to 12% if we pin 8 layers. We can do dynamic eviction for cold sessions.

[00:08:26] Maya: sounds workable. Okay last section — experiments matrix. we'll run: (1) per-layer perturbation, (2) int8-gptq vs awq vs fp8 baselines, (3) canary mixed-precision rollout with KV trace reproduction, (4) converter parity. We'll capture logits, PPL, and user-facing metrics for the clinical task. Connor to send scripts + plotting notebook.

[00:08:58] Ravi: thanks. anything else?

[00:09:02] Elena: minor — we've seen one case where the transcription had "K-V cash" in logs but it was actually KV cache; small typo but might confuse devs.

[00:09:09] Connor: haha noted, will fix.

[00:09:12] Maya: perfect. recap of next steps in chat, we'll follow-up with links. thanks everyone.
